Professor Rajiv Ranjan
🎤 Keynote Speaker

University Chair Professor, IoT, School of Computing, Newcastle University
Professor Rajiv Ranjan is an Australian-British computer scientist, of Indian origin, known for his research in Distributed Systems (Cloud Computing, Big Data, and the Internet of Things). He is University Chair Professor for the Internet of Things research in the School of Computing of Newcastle University, United Kingdom. He is also Director of the Centre of AI Safety at Newcastle University. He is an internationally established scientist in the area of Distributed Systems (having published about 350 scientific papers). He is a fellow of IEEE (2024), Academia Europaea (2022) and the Asia-Pacific Artificial Intelligence Association (2023). He is also the Founding Director of the International Centre (UK-Australia) on the EV Security and National Edge Artificial Intelligence Hub, both funded by EPSRC. He has secured more than $68 Million AUD (£34 Million+ GBP) in the form of competitive research grants from both public and private agencies. He is an innovator with strong and sustained academic and industrial impact and a globally recognized R&D leader with a proven track record. He serves on the editorial boards of top quality international journals including IEEE Transactions on Computers (2014-2016), IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing, ACM Transactions on the Internet of Things, The Computer (Oxford University), and The Computing (Springer) and Future Generation Computer Systems. He led the Blue Skies section (department, 2014-2019) of IEEE Cloud Computing, where his principal role was to identify and write about the most important, cutting-edge research issues at the intersection of multiple, inter-dependent research disciplines within distributed systems research area including Internet of Things, Big Data Analytics, Cloud Computing, and Edge Computing. He is one of the highly cited authors in computer science and software engineering worldwide (h-index=88+, g-index=330+, and 37500+ google scholar citations, h-index=67+ and 20500+ Scopus citations, and h-index=52+ and 12700+ Web of Science citations).

Dr. Muhammad Usman Hadi

Assistant Professor, Ulster University, Belfast
Dr Usman Hadi is a Lecturer in Engineering at Ulster University and CEO of Drone Sentinel Inc., specialising in 5G/6G communications, AI and cybersecurity for autonomous systems. He holds a PhD in Electronic Engineering from the University of Bologna, Italy, and previously held research positions at Aalborg University, Denmark and Nokia Bell Labs. With over 5000 citations, he has authored over 100 research publications. As Principal Investigator, he has received funding from EPSRC, Innovate U.K, Digital Twin Network Plus, DARe Hub, British Council, Garfield Weston Trust, Belfast City Council Advanced Connectivity Technologies Grant, and International Science Partnership Funds. He has been included in the top 2% of researchers for five consecutive years, since 2021. Dr Hadi is also a recipient of the Pitch of the Year Award from CYBERASAP Year 10 cohort. His research interests include cybersecurity for VANETs, machine learning for engineering applications, autonomous aerial vehicles, fiber wireless communications, microwave photonics, and devices for telecommunications.

Dr. Aditya Japa

Lecturer, Ulster University, Derry/Londonderry
Aditya Japa received Ph.D. degree in Electronics and Communication Engineering, from Dr. SPM IIIT Naya Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India in 2021, with a focus on Emerging Technologies for Hardware security. After his Ph.D., he worked as Research Fellow with Centre for Secure Information Technologies (CSIT), Queen’s University Belfast, U.K. He is currently working as a Lecturer with School of Computing, Engineering and Intelligent Systems, Ulster University, Derry, UK. His research mainly focuses on Hardware and System Security. Specifically, he is into the design of PUF and TRNG design. He worked on emerging/beyond CMOS based security strategies, power side-channel analysis, and countermeasures. His current research interests include the design of PUFs Security in/for approximate computing and Security of Neural Network Accelerators.

title: Securing Edge AI Workshop
text:
About the Workshop
Connected devices are embedded throughout our homes, cars, factories, and critical infrastructure, yet device security has often taken a backseat to other considerations, such as power management and latency. As the prevalence of edge devices increases, security challenges, such as resource efficient cryptography, securing over-the-air updates, and defending against side-channel attacks, need to be addressed. This workshop aims to inform participants about the risks to edge devices and provide the tools to defend against them.

Workshop Topics

How AI is changing the Cybersecurity Landscape: Are the new tools introducing new threats?
Threat modelling for constrained device: Identify and mitigate security risks at the edge.
Lightweight cryptographic protocols: Secure communications and authentication with minimal overhead.
Secure firmware & OTA updates: Protect device integrity with secure boot and update strategies.
Edge network intrusion detection: Detect anomalies and attacks in resource-constrained networks.

title: Organisers
text:
Seán Ó Fithcheallaigh

PhD Researcher, School of Computing, Ulster University.
Seán is a PhD Researcher within the Pervasive Computing Research Centre (PCRC), specialising in Federated Learning (FL) with a focus on developing trustworthy FL frameworks for sensor networks and IoT devices. He is also a researcher with the BT Ireland Innovation Centre (BTIIC), where he works on IoT Autonomics. With over a decade of experience in electronics and software engineering, including developing next-generation application-specific IoT sensors, he brings first-hand understanding of the practical constraints and opportunities that shape AI deployment at the edge.
Contact:  o_fithcheallaigh-s@ulster.ac.uk








Dr Ian Cleland

Reader/Research Director, School of Computing, Ulster University.
Ian is a Reader in the School of Computing at Ulster University, where he serves as Research Director. His work focuses on applied AI, machine learning, and intelligent sensing technologies. He has over 15 years’ experience developing real-world AI systems across healthcare and digital innovation. Ian’s research interests include Edge AI, sensor-based activity recognition, wearable and embedded technologies, and the use of synthetic data to support data-driven modelling. He is particularly interested in how AI can move closer to the edge to enable scalable, privacy-aware, and real-time intelligent systems. He received degrees in Biomedical Engineering and Computer Science from Ulster University and has published more than 100 peer-reviewed research papers in AI, digital health, and health informatics. Ian has contributed to over £20M in externally funded research projects, including major collaborations with industry through initiatives such as the Connected Health Innovation Centre (CHIC) and the PwC Advanced Engineering and Research Centre (ARC).








Dr Jose Santos

Deputy Head of School of Computing, Ulster University
Dr Jose A. Santos (PhD, SFHEA) is Deputy Head of the School of Computing at Ulster University’s Belfast campus. With a background in Electronic Engineering and over two decades of academic and research experience, his research interest focuses on developing intelligent, sensor‑driven systems that monitor and improve the environmental conditions people experience in homes, workplaces and public buildings. His work explores how IoT‑based sensing platforms, combined with machine learning models, can provide continuous, fine‑grained insights into indoor and outdoor pollutant levels, ventilation effectiveness, heat distribution and personal comfort requirements. He is particularly interested in fusing heterogeneous sensor streams to create adaptive, real‑time control mechanisms that mitigate poor air quality, optimise thermal comfort and reduce energy waste. His research aims to deliver practical, human‑centred solutions that enhance wellbeing, support independent living and inform healthier building design through predictive analytics, environmental modelling and autonomous intervention technologies.
